heroSupport: Fuse the alert, rank progenitors, draft the follow-up — before the light.
aboutTagline: Neutrinos arrive first. We aim telescopes before the light.
aboutLead: When a nearby star dies, a neutrino burst can reach Earth minutes to hours ahead of optical shock breakout. Project Supernova turns that head start into a sky localization, a ranked list of likely progenitor stars, and live alerts observers can act on — before the flash.
aboutDoes1: Ingests supernova / high-energy neutrino alerts (cached IceCube & galactic CCSN replays offline; live GCN / SNEWS-style channels when configured).
aboutDoes2: Draws a localization on an all-sky map and ranks stars inside the area of interest against a precomputed literature inventory.
aboutDoes3: Pushes ranked ICRS coordinates to anyone who Subscribes to events — campus scopes and backyard instruments included — over a live WebSocket.
aboutHonesty: No invented bibcodes. Simulated runs wear a Simulated badge. Community packages are follow-up helpers, not official GCN notices.
aboutWhyBody: Core collapse releases neutrinos promptly; the explosion shock still has to climb through the stellar envelope before light escapes. That gap is the race: localize, prioritize known massive stars, and get coordinates onto real instruments while the optical breakout window is still open. Class-dependent models put that window from tens of seconds (compact WR) to about a day (some RSG cases) — estimates, not countdown clocks for any one star.
aboutDemo1: Cold start listens (live_waiting); full Yale BSC5 sky, empty ranked list. Nothing auto-plays.
aboutDemo2: Run IceCube-170922A or the galactic CCSN / Betelgeuse scenario from the event cards.
aboutDemo3: Dual red outlines appear; the view zooms to the outer aperture; field + ranked stars light up.
aboutDemo4: Posterior-sorted candidates with class life window, confidence, and ADS-backed evidence where the index already has it.
aboutDemo5: Mint access + refresh tokens, open the subscribe WebSocket, watch the next candidate package land.
aboutCalHacksBody: Clear problem → working demo path → measurable surface (skymap, ranking, subscribe). End-to-end in one loop: alert → localization → ranked stars → actionable feed. Stack: FastAPI + Vite/TypeScript, SVG Mollweide skymap, offline progenitor inventory, WebSocket community alerts.
aboutSpaceXBody: Real astrophysics data paths: SNEWS-style timing, IceCube historical alerts, Yale BSC5 sky field. Latency is the product — neutrino lead time becomes follow-up urgency. Actionable alerts for human observers: coordinates on the wire, not a slideshow.

subscribeHint: Get ranked ICRS targets the moment Project Supernova localizes a burst — over a live WebSocket.
subscribeHonesty: Not official GCN. Packages set simulated=true when applicable; ADS bibcodes only if already on the candidate. Success confirms token issue + WS connect — not email delivery.
subscribeFailed: Subscribe failed — rate-limited or server error; try again later.
subscribeWsExpired: WebSocket closed — access token expired (refresh & reconnect).
subscribeWsExtended: Access extended on the live WebSocket.
subscribeRefreshFailed: Refresh failed — click Get tokens & connect again.
subscribeOpen: Open access: no account and no prior credentials. Anyone can POST /subscribe to mint tokens and connect.
subscribeDocsIssueBody: POST /subscribe (empty JSON is fine). Returns a short-lived access_token and a longer-lived refresh_token. Tokens are hashed at rest.
subscribeDocsRefreshBody: POST /subscribe/refresh with your refresh_token before access expires. Send the new access_token on the live WebSocket to extend the session.
subscribeDocsWsBody: Connect to /ws/subscribe?access_token=…. Server pushes community_alert frames. If access expires without a refresh, the socket closes with code 4001.
subscribeDocsRelayHint: Copy this prompt into your own AI to generate a Python listener that refreshes tokens and relays ranked alerts on a channel you choose. Community follow-up only — not an official GCN notice.
